<thought>The spectrum shows a clear M+1 peak (~8 % of the base) consistent with the natural 13C abundance, indicating the presence of carbon. The M+2 peak (~8 % of the base) matches the expected ~4 % per sulfur atom, suggesting at least one sulfur (likely two). No 3:1 or 1:1 M+2 patterns for chlorine or bromine are observed. Therefore, the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
